rounds.title: Root comment boundary
rounds.interviewerPrompt: Start with a normalized root insertion that does not mutate the existing tree.
constraints: Trim the draft and reject an empty or whitespace-only comment.
Append a valid root node with a stable unique ID and an empty children array.
Clear the root draft only after a successful insertion.
Preserve every existing node and its relative order.

frameworkTests.name: Round 1 · Valid root insertion preserves the tree

rounds.title: Single reply owner
rounds.interviewerPrompt: Bind reply composition to one comment identity at a time.
constraints: Clicking Reply opens exactly one editor beneath that comment.
Opening another editor transfers ownership instead of duplicating drafts.
Cancel closes the editor and clears its draft.
Submitting a non-empty reply inserts it under the owning parent and closes the editor.

frameworkTests.name: Round 2 · Reply is inserted under its owner

rounds.title: Arbitrary-depth update
rounds.interviewerPrompt: Apply a recursive path update without mutating ancestors or losing siblings.
constraints: Locate parents by stable ID at any depth rather than by a hard-coded level.
Rebuild only the ancestor path to the changed node.
Preserve every unaffected branch by value and order.
Generate globally unique IDs for nested and root nodes.

frameworkTests.name: Round 3 · Replying to a reply creates a third level

rounds.title: Accessible tree and focus
rounds.interviewerPrompt: Expose recursive structure and return focus predictably after editing.
constraints: Expose the comment list as a tree and every comment as a treeitem with its one-based aria-level.
Give each Reply control an accessible name that identifies its comment.
Give the reply input a stable label associated with the owning comment.
After Post or Cancel, return focus to the Reply control that opened the editor.
Announce successful insertion in a polite status region without moving reading position.

frameworkTests.name: Round 4 · Recursive structure and insertion are announced
